caption: The drawing depicts a monochromatic, black-and-white illustration of a three-tiered bell tower, featuring a total of five arched openings—one at the topmost tier, two at the middle tier, and two at the lowest arched level—with the structure sitting atop a rectangular base made of brick-like patterns. The detailing on the drawing uses stippling and fine lines to create texture and shading, particularly on the bricks and weathered surfaces, giving the impression of patches of worn or damaged stone. Beneath the structure, a banner contains the handwritten text “1769” on the left and “Misión San Diego de Alcalá” across the bottom. The overall composition is centered on an off-white background with no additional objects or scenery.
title: Mision San Diego de Alcala
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
